correctness.rationale: For the canonical p+1 quadratic-chirp/coordinate bases at every odd prime p, completing the square in the quadratic Gauss sum gives normalized overlaps epsilon_p chi(bprime-b) zeta^(-(aprime-a)^2/[4(bprime-b)]). For three finite distinct basis labels the Bargmann phase is epsilon_p³ chi(B) zeta^(D²/(4B)) with B product of three nonzero basis-label differences and D a nonzero affine-linear combination of three vector labels. For the computational-basis case a cyclic rotation gives epsilon_p³ chi(-db) zeta^(-db(t+da/(2db))²). In both cases the exponent-zero signs can be ± while exponent s nonzero forces the sign chi(s); these p+1 distinct phases do not collide for odd p. Every value of the D-linear form has p² preimages. Multiplying finite basis labels by a nonresidue bijects ordered distinct-basis triples and reverses the zero-exponent sign, so zero phases occur C/2 each and nonzero exponent phases C each, C=p³(p²−1), total pC=p⁴(p²−1). For H=sqrt(p)(G−I), tr H=0, tr H²=6 and det H=2Re(tau), hence eigenvalue cubic lambda³−3lambda−2Re(tau)=0. Pairing conjugate s and −s gives (p+3)/2 spectral types for p=1 mod4 and (p+1)/2 for p=3 mod4. Direct same-basis and two-same-basis Gram cases account for the remaining ordered triples. Independently enumerated exact symbolic Gauss exponents and signs for every labeled three-distinct-basis triple at p=3,5,7,11 (648, 15000, 115248, 1756920 cases) and matched each full histogram; finite enumerations supplement the all-prime field-count proof.

originality.rationale: Quadratic Gauss-sum MUB constructions (Klappenecker–Rötteler 2003, Theorem 2.2) are classical and explicitly excluded from novelty. The recent MUB triple-products study (Gültekin–Samuel–Gedik 2026) tabulates numerical phases/frequencies only for dimensions 3,4,5; those particular counts are not claimed new. The submitted symbolic uniform formula for EVERY odd prime, its exact nonzero-base-triple multiplicities and Gram spectral-type count requires the field-square counting argument, not just the existence of MUBs or small numerical histograms. Other Resultary chirp/Gabor phase findings concern different invariants. Best-of-knowledge O remains subject to finite-geometric/Clifford orbit aliases.
residual_risks: Finite-geometry or Clifford-orbit association schemes may encode an equivalent all-prime triple-product distribution under different notation.
